hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext:
nutmeg (football data analytics) is installed. When a task involves football data:
- Provider facts (IDs, qualifiers, field names, endpoints, coordinate systems, coverage, rate limits) come from the football-docs tools, never from memory. Name the doc you used. If the docs do not cover it, say so. If the football-docs tools are not available, say so, give the install line `claude mcp add football-docs -- npx -y football-docs@0.16.1`, and label any provider fact you give anyway "unverified (from memory)".
- Player, team and match IDs come from the Reep Register (resolve_entity) or the user's data, never from memory. Join providers on IDs, not names, and report unmatched rows.
- Before judging a player or team from a stat, check that the stat can support the claim: per 90 with a minimum-minutes filter, enough sample, possession adjustment for defensive counts, post-shot xG instead of save percentage, no distance as proof of effort, no with-or-without win rates, no one-season finishing verdicts.
- For analysis the user will publish or decide on (a shortlist, a match or opposition report, a memo, a chart or thread for social media), start a research project so every number keeps its evidence: load /nutmeg:research, or run `python3 "@PLUGIN_ROOT@/core/nutmeg.py" new <slug> --question "<question>"` and follow its messages. Quick questions, lookups and code fixes stay outside projects.
- Inside an active research project (research/.active exists): run analysis files with `python3 "@PLUGIN_ROOT@/core/nutmeg.py" run <file> --input <data>` as a command on its own, so the user sees the code and inputs before it runs; record every number, provider fact, ID and citation that goes into an output with `python3 "@PLUGIN_ROOT@/core/nutmeg.py" claim add`; give each plan choice a one-sentence reason.
- For fetching, cleaning, metrics, analysis, charts or code review, load the matching nutmeg skill.
